points.description: States that the star (*) operator returns an alias/synonym for (i.e. the object itself, or the value/object at) what its operand points to in memory — the object the pointer points to.
points.partial_credit: Half or more of the marks if it says it gives the value/object pointed to but vaguely or with a minor error (e.g. says it returns the address stored in the pointer's target without mentioning the object/value).

points.description: Names the star operator as the dereferencing (indirection) operator.
points.partial_credit: Award in full if the term dereference/indirection is used or clearly described as following a pointer to what it points to.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the operator returns the object/value that the pointer operand points to (alias or the thing itself), in any wording, and ideally calling it dereferencing. Part marks for vague or slightly wrong statements, such as mentioning pointers and memory without clearly saying it returns the pointed-to object. No marks for saying it returns the address or the pointer itself, or for talking only about declaring pointers or multiplication.
